summary: ESR measures how fast red cells settle in a tube, which changes with the proteins inflammation produces. It moves more slowly than CRP in both directions, so the two together show whether inflammation is new or long-standing.
what_it_measures: The distance red blood cells fall in one hour in a standing column, reported in mm/hr.

interpretations.meaning: A raised ESR indicates inflammation, but it also rises with age, anaemia and pregnancy, so it is less specific than CRP.

when_to_seek_help: A very high ESR with headache, scalp tenderness or jaw pain can indicate giant cell arteritis, which needs urgent assessment.
approved_by: Demo dataset (illustrative values, not for clinical use)
